Therefore, sponsors should consult the Division 379 before initiating a neuraxial block drug product development program for a local anesthetic drug 380 product with prolonged duration of effect. 381

candidates.statement: For purposes of this guidance, a fixed-combination drug product (FCDP) is one in which two or 385 more active ingredients are combined at a fixed dosage in a single dosage form. When 386 developing an FCDP, the sponsor must demonstrate that each active ingredient makes a 387 contribution to the claimed effect of the combination drug product, as defined in 21 CFR 300.50. 388 The demonstration of such contribution may require a properly designed factorial trial. In 389 addition, the benefit of the proposed combination of active ingredients must outweigh any 390 additional risk posed by the combination. 11 , 12

candidates.statement: The recommended primary efficacy endpoint for the evaluation of the postoperative analgesic 408 effect of a local anesthetic drug product is the AUC of pain scores. The clinical pain scale(s) 409 utilized to assess pain should be validated in the patient population(s) being studied. The 410 schedule of assessments should be appropriate to evaluate the clinical endpoints and reflect the 411 PK and PD profiles of the proposed local anesthetic drug product. Because the PK and PD 412 profile may vary with each drug product, it is necessary to demonstrate superiority or 413 noninferiority relative to the comparator during the entire proposed duration of effect, most 414 importantly the later time points. 415

candidates.statement: For a claim of superiority in the prescribing information, the sponsor needs to demonstrate that 506 the proposed local anesthetic drug product is superior to an approved drug product from both 507 statistical and clinical perspectives using clinically relevant efficacy or safety endpoints in 508 replicated adequate and well-controlled trials making direct comparison to the approved drug 509 product for each proposed indication. 14 In addition, to claim superiority, the sponsor must 510 establish a positive benefit-risk profile of the proposed product compared to the approved drug 511 product. 512

candidates.statement: Sponsors should support novel endpoints with data demonstrating that the endpoints represent a 526 clinically meaningful benefit. For endpoints related to the reduction in 529 opioid analgesic drug products use, opioid-sparing claims, and data needed to support such 530 claims, sponsors should refer to the draft guidance for industry Development of Non-Opioid 531 Analgesics for Acute Pain (February 2022). 16
candidates.context: There is great public health interest in assessing additional, clinically meaningful endpoints such 516 as reduction in hospitalization or rehospitalization, emergency department visits, or death caused 517 by opioid abuse, as well as improvements in the ability to resume work, school, or other 518 productive activities. FDA recognizes that evaluating these outcomes could require larger trials 519 than those usually conducted for marketing approval.
